name: Bernd Lange-Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on applying a generalised scheme of tariff preferences and repealing Regulation (EU) No 978/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on a new EU trade scheme that lets poorer countries sell goods to Europe with lower or no import taxes. It asks for stricter conditions: countries must ratify and actually apply international conventions on human rights, labour, environment and good governance. It adds a monitoring process, a public plan of action for countries seeking extra benefits, and makes withdrawing preferences a last resort after dialogue.

- Countries getting standard preferences must ratify listed conventions within five years, or preferences can be suspended.
- Countries seeking extra benefits must publish a time-bound plan of action, monitored with civil society input.
- Withdrawal of preferences becomes a last resort, after a year of "enhanced engagement" and dialogue.
